original_question: Do there exist nontrivial pairs of maps L and R such that the rooted binary tree z -> (L(z), R(z)) lists every positive rational number exactly once, analogously to the classical Calkin-Wilf tree? More ambitiously, can one classify all such functional pairs?
target_in_paper: 2012.3 Problem Session III (Jerry Hu's question, p. 20): generalizing the Calkin-Wilf tree by asking for other binary trees of the form z with children L(z) and R(z) in which every positive rational appears exactly once.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's main point very closely: it asks for binary trees generated by two maps L and R, modeled on the classical Calkin-Wilf tree, whose vertices are exactly the positive rational numbers with no repetitions, and it also reflects the paper's stronger follow-up of finding all such nontrivial pairs.
missing_details: The paper implicitly works with maps L,R from the positive rationals to the positive rationals; this domain and codomain should be stated explicitly.
The rooted tree should be specified as the infinite binary tree obtained by starting from the root 1 and recursively assigning to each vertex z the two children L(z) and R(z).
To make the comparison with the classical Calkin-Wilf tree self-contained, the classical pair should be named explicitly: L_0(z)=z/(z+1) and R_0(z)=z+1, equivalently a/b maps to a/(a+b) and (a+b)/b.
The phrase 'lists every positive rational number exactly once' should be formalized as: the set of vertices is exactly Q_{>0}, and each element of Q_{>0} occurs at a unique vertex.

The paper does not impose extra structural assumptions on L and R such as being linear fractional, polynomial, matrix-generated, or monotone; adding such hypotheses would narrow the scope beyond the stated question.
The word 'nontrivial' is left implicit in the paper; for a stand-alone formulation it is best interpreted minimally as meaning 'different from the classical Calkin-Wilf pair'.
refined_question: Besides the classical Calkin-Wilf pair L_0(z)=z/(z+1) and R_0(z)=z+1 (equivalently, a/b maps to a/(a+b) and (a+b)/b), do there exist maps L,R from the set Q_{>0} of positive rational numbers to itself such that the infinite rooted binary tree obtained from the root 1 by giving each vertex z the two children L(z) and R(z) has vertex set exactly Q_{>0}, with each positive rational occurring once and only once? If so, can one determine all such nontrivial pairs L,R, or at least exhibit any example other than the classical Calkin-Wilf pair?
justification: This is the nearest paper-faithful formulation of your draft. In Section 2012.3, after recalling the classical Calkin-Wilf tree and stating that when a=b=1 each positive rational appears exactly once, the paper asks whether there are other trees of the form z with children L(z) and R(z) having the same uniqueness-and-exhaustion property, and whether one can find all, or any, nontrivial functional pairs. The refinement above only makes explicit the root, the domain/codomain Q_{>0}, the classical example being excluded, and the precise meaning of 'appears exactly once'; it does not add restrictions absent from the paper. Section 2014.3.1 supplies the convenient z-notation for the classical Calkin-Wilf maps, writing the parent-to-children rule as z maps to z/(z+1) and z+1 and again noting that starting from root 1 every fraction occurs exactly once.
